title: Trombone idols and playing bass for Ted Lewis
summary: Netto names Teagarden and George Brunis as favorites and recalls being Ted Lewis's bass player in New Orleans, including Lewis's dice gambling.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Did you have any real idols when you were beginning to play? I mean, anybody that you admired, any trombonists? Like you listened to on a record or an impression, either one?
Well, T. Gordon, you know, everybody liked him. Everybody liked T. Gordon. Do you remember George Brunis? George Brunis?
Do you remember George Brunis? Oh yeah, I remember George, yeah. George. Well, George with Ted Lewis.

In fact I played with Ted Lewis down in the room there. But George wasn't there then. George had left him. He came down to New Orleans and he stayed by, and he went over to the Gulf Coast there, with a couple of bands. In fact I played a couple of jobs with him on the bass fiddle, you know, and he was playing some ball. George was not on, he didn't read music. He didn't know anything about music. In fact, who in the world was a worse pirate player than Ted Lewis. Sorry. He was fierce. And I was his official bass player. Whenever he came around in the air, Solly Klein used to run his band for him. Yeah, the violin player.
Yeah, the violin player. And he used to send me a telegram. He was coming in the blue room on such and such a day. Be sure and be there.
Well, Ted Lewis hired good musicians, he should take that out of the house. He really did that.

Well, sometimes when he came in later on with the bands there, sometimes some of them weren't too good, you know. He didn't care much then. The only thing is, but he still loved to gamble, you know. He went over there. He held up the show for about 45 minutes one night. He was shooting dice in the one, two, three across the street from Roosevelt, and they sent for him over there, come on, the show's coming on. He said, wait a minute, I've got to make this eight. He went that eight and the shower door, and his wife used to travel with him. And she says, you have to pay the band. Because the band got their money, she had to take the band's money, and he says, no, the rest of it you can do what you want with it. But because Sally Klein threw him in, on Vegas, he says, over there, he says, he lost all of the salary, the band there, and what you call it, they had it sitting, freezing out there in the bus station waiting for New York to send them the money. Next morning, they couldn't get to New York at night time, so the office was closed, so they sent them the money the next morning.
